courseDetails.title: Elementary Mathematics II (Calculus)
courseDetails.description: A 100-level foundation course covering real-valued functions, limits, continuity, differentiation, integration, improper integrals, areas, volumes of revolution, and practical applications of calculus.

questions.question: Which statement correctly defines a function?
options: The domain and range must always be identical.
Each output must be assigned to exactly one input.
Each input in the domain is assigned exactly one output.
Every input must be assigned to two or more outputs.
questions.explanation: A function may send different inputs to the same output, but each input must have exactly one output.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between functions and relations?
options: Functions and relations are completely unrelated.
A relation must assign exactly one output to each input.
Every function is a relation, but not every relation is a function.
questions.explanation: A relation is any set of ordered pairs. It is a function only when no input is paired with more than one output.

questions.question: If f(x) = 2x + 3, what is f(4)?
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 4: f(4) = 2(4) + 3 = 11.

questions.question: What is the domain of f(x) = x² + 3x + 2?
questions.explanation: A polynomial is defined for every real value of x.

questions.question: What is the domain of f(x) = 5/(x - 3)?
questions.explanation: The denominator must not be zero. Since x - 3 = 0 at x = 3, that value is excluded.

questions.question: What is the domain of h(x) = √(x + 2)?
questions.explanation: For a real square root, x + 2 ≥ 0, so x ≥ -2.

questions.question: What is the range of f(x) = 2x - 9?
questions.explanation: A non-constant linear function can produce every real output.

questions.question: What is the range of g(x) = 3/(x + 8)?
questions.explanation: The numerator is nonzero, so g(x) can never equal 0. Every other real output is possible.

questions.question: What is the range of f(x) = 2 - |x - 3|?
questions.explanation: Because |x - 3| ≥ 0, 2 - |x - 3| ≤ 2. The maximum output is 2.

questions.question: If f(x) = 3x - 7, what is f⁻¹(x)?
questions.explanation: Let y = 3x - 7, interchange x and y, and solve: x = 3y - 7, so y = (x + 7)/3.

questions.question: Given f(x) = 5x - 4 and g(x) = x², what is (f ∘ g)(x)?
Given f(x) = 5x - 4 and g(x) = x², what is (g ∘ f)(x)?
What does the vertical line test determine?
options: Whether a line has positive slope
Whether a graph represents a function of x
questions.explanation: A graph represents y as a function of x when every vertical line intersects it at most once.

questions.question: A function that is both one-to-one and onto is called what?
questions.explanation: A bijection is simultaneously injective and surjective.

questions.question: For the line f(x) = -3x + 5, what are the slope and y-intercept?
questions.explanation: In f(x) = mx + b, m is the slope and b is the y-intercept.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the graph of f(x) = -2x² + 3x + 1?
options: It is a parabola opening downward.
It is an exponential decay curve.
It is a parabola opening upward.
questions.explanation: The coefficient of x² is negative, so the parabola opens downward.

questions.question: Which function represents exponential decay?
questions.explanation: An exponential function bˣ represents decay when 0 < b < 1.

questions.question: The logarithmic function log_b(x) is the inverse of which function?
questions.explanation: Exponentiation and logarithms with the same base undo each other.

questions.question: In a right triangle, tan θ equals which ratio?
questions.explanation: By SOH-CAH-TOA, tangent is opposite divided by adjacent.

questions.question: For f(x) = {2x + 1 if x ≤ 0; x² - 3 if x > 0}, what is f(2)?
What is the vertex of y = |x - 3|?
questions.explanation: The graph of y = |x - h| has vertex (h, 0), so the vertex is (3, 0).

questions.question: What is the degree of p(x) = -x³ + 3x² - 2?
questions.explanation: The degree is the highest exponent of x with a nonzero coefficient.

questions.question: What does lim(x→a) f(x) = L mean?
options: f(x) is undefined for all x near a.
f(x) approaches L as x approaches a.
x approaches L as f(x) approaches a.
questions.explanation: A limit describes the value approached by the function as the input approaches a specified point.

questions.question: Evaluate lim(x→2) (3x + 1).
questions.explanation: Linear functions are continuous, so substitute x = 2: 3(2) + 1 = 7.

questions.question: Evaluate lim(x→3) (x² - 9)/(x - 3).
questions.explanation: Factor x² - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3). Cancel x - 3, then evaluate x + 3 at x = 3 to get 6.

questions.question: Evaluate lim(x→0) (√(x + 4) - 2)/x.
questions.explanation: Rationalise: the expression becomes 1/(√(x + 4) + 2), which tends to 1/4.

questions.question: A two-sided limit lim(x→a) f(x) exists when which condition holds?
options: The graph must cross the x-axis at a.
The left-hand limit must be greater than the right-hand limit.
The left-hand and right-hand limits both exist and are equal.
questions.explanation: A finite two-sided limit exists only when both one-sided limits approach the same value.

questions.question: If lim(x→2⁻) f(x) = 3 and lim(x→2⁺) f(x) = 5, what can be concluded?
options: The function is continuous at x = 2.
questions.explanation: The one-sided limits are unequal, so the two-sided limit does not exist.

questions.question: Evaluate lim(x→∞) (5x² + 1)/(2x² - 3).
questions.explanation: The numerator and denominator have the same degree, so the limit is the ratio of leading coefficients, 5/2.

questions.question: Evaluate lim(x→∞) (3x + 4)/(x² + 1).
questions.explanation: The denominator has higher degree than the numerator, so the fraction approaches 0.

questions.question: Using L'Hôpital's rule, evaluate lim(x→0) (eˣ - 1)/x.
questions.explanation: The form is 0/0. Differentiate numerator and denominator: eˣ/1, which gives 1 at x = 0.

questions.question: Which three conditions are required for f to be continuous at x = a?
options: f(a) exists, lim(x→a)f(x) exists, and lim(x→a)f(x) = f(a)
The graph has a vertical asymptote at a
f(a) = 0, f'(a) exists, and f is increasing
questions.explanation: Continuity requires the function value and the two-sided limit to exist and be equal.

questions.question: The function f(x) = (x² - 1)/(x - 1) has what type of discontinuity at x = 1?
questions.explanation: After cancellation, f(x) behaves like x + 1 except for a hole at x = 1, so the discontinuity is removable.

questions.question: A piecewise function has left-hand limit 2 and right-hand limit 7 at x = 0. What type of discontinuity occurs?
questions.explanation: Different finite one-sided limits create a jump discontinuity.

questions.question: What type of discontinuity does f(x) = 1/(x - 4) have at x = 4?
questions.explanation: The function has a vertical asymptote at x = 4, and its values grow without bound.

questions.question: Let f(x) = {x + 1 if x < 2; k if x = 2; 3x - 3 if x > 2}. What value of k makes f continuous at x = 2?
questions.explanation: The left limit is 2 + 1 = 3 and the right limit is 3(2) - 3 = 3, so f(2) must be 3.

questions.question: If a graph approaches y = 4 from both sides as x approaches 1, but the plotted point is at (1, 7), what is lim(x→1) f(x)?
questions.explanation: The limit depends on nearby behaviour, not the actual plotted value at x = 1.

questions.question: What does the derivative f'(a) represent geometrically?
options: The slope of the tangent line to y = f(x) at x = a
The area under the curve up to a
The average value of f on every interval
questions.explanation: The derivative at a point is the instantaneous rate of change and the tangent-line slope.

questions.question: Using first principles, what is the derivative of f(x) = x²?
questions.explanation: f'(x) = lim(h→0)[(x+h)² - x²]/h = lim(h→0)(2x + h) = 2x.

questions.question: Differentiate f(x) = 4x⁵ - 3x² + 7.
questions.explanation: Apply the power rule term by term: d(4x⁵)/dx = 20x⁴ and d(-3x²)/dx = -6x.

questions.question: Differentiate y = (x² + 1)(x³ - 2).
questions.explanation: By the product rule, (uv)' = u'v + uv'.

questions.question: Differentiate y = (x² + 1)/x.
questions.explanation: Using the quotient rule gives [2x·x - (x² + 1)]/x² = (x² - 1)/x².

questions.question: Differentiate y = (3x + 1)⁴.
questions.explanation: Use the chain rule: 4(3x + 1)³ multiplied by the derivative of 3x + 1, which is 3.

questions.question: Differentiate y = e^(2x).
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, d(e^u)/dx = e^u u'; here u = 2x, so u' = 2.

questions.question: Differentiate y = sin x.
questions.explanation: The standard derivative of sin x is cos x.

questions.question: Differentiate y = cos x.
questions.explanation: The standard derivative of cos x is -sin x.

questions.question: Differentiate y = ln x.
questions.explanation: For x > 0, d(ln x)/dx = 1/x.

questions.question: If x² + y² = 25, what is dy/dx?
questions.explanation: Differentiate implicitly: 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0, so dy/dx = -x/y.

questions.question: For f(x) = x³ - 2x, what is f'(2)?
What is the equation of the tangent to y = x² at x = 2?
questions.explanation: At x = 2, the point is (2,4) and the slope is 2x = 4. Thus y - 4 = 4(x - 2).

questions.question: What is the second derivative of f(x) = x⁴ - 3x²?
questions.explanation: First derivative: 4x³ - 6x. Differentiate again to get 12x² - 6.

questions.question: What is the third derivative of f(x) = 2x⁵?
If s(t) is position, which derivative represents velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity is the first derivative of position with respect to time.

questions.question: If s(t) is position, which derivative represents acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, so it is the second derivative of position.

questions.question: The third derivative of position with respect to time is commonly called what?
questions.explanation: Jerk measures the rate of change of acceleration.

questions.question: For f(x) = x² - 4x + 1, at what x-value is the stationary point?
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 2x - 4. Set f'(x)=0: 2x - 4 = 0, giving x = 2.

questions.question: If f'(x) > 0 throughout an interval, what does this imply?
options: f is discontinuous on that interval.
f is decreasing on that interval.
f is constant on that interval.
f is increasing on that interval.
questions.explanation: A positive derivative means the function rises as x increases.

questions.question: If f''(x) > 0 on an interval, the graph is described as what?
questions.explanation: A positive second derivative indicates that the slope is increasing, so the curve is concave upward.

questions.question: For f(x) = x³ - 3x, what are the critical points?
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 3x² - 3 = 3(x² - 1). Setting it to zero gives x = ±1.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫ x⁴ dx.
questions.explanation: By the power rule, ∫xⁿdx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C, so ∫x⁴dx = x⁵/5 + C.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫(3x² - 4) dx.
questions.explanation: Integrate term by term: ∫3x²dx = x³ and ∫-4dx = -4x.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫₀² x dx.
questions.explanation: An antiderivative is x²/2. Evaluating from 0 to 2 gives 4/2 = 2.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫ x e^(x²) dx.
questions.explanation: Let u = x², so du = 2x dx. The integral becomes (1/2)∫e^u du = (1/2)e^(x²) + C.

questions.question: Using integration by parts, evaluate ∫ x eˣ dx.
questions.explanation: Choose u=x and dv=eˣdx. Then ∫u dv = uv - ∫v du = xeˣ - eˣ + C.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫ sec²x dx.
questions.explanation: Since d(tan x)/dx = sec²x, the antiderivative is tan x + C.

questions.question: Which partial-fraction decomposition is correct for 1/(x² - 1)?
questions.explanation: Since x² - 1 = (x - 1)(x + 1), solving for constants gives 1/2 and -1/2.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫₋₁¹ x³ dx.
questions.explanation: x³ is odd, and the integral of an odd function over a symmetric interval [-a,a] is 0.

questions.question: Find the area under y = x² from x = 0 to x = 3.
questions.explanation: Area = ∫₀³x²dx = [x³/3]₀³ = 27/3 = 9.

questions.question: Find the area between y = 4 - x² and the x-axis from x = -2 to x = 2.
questions.explanation: Area = ∫₋₂²(4 - x²)dx = [4x - x³/3]₋₂² = 32/3.

questions.question: According to the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, d/dx[∫₀ˣ f(t)dt] equals what?
questions.explanation: The derivative of an accumulation function with variable upper limit is the integrand evaluated at that limit.

questions.question: Why is the constant C included in an indefinite integral?
options: It converts an indefinite integral into a derivative.
Different antiderivatives can differ by a constant.
questions.explanation: The derivative of any constant is zero, so a family of antiderivatives differs by an arbitrary constant.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫ 2x(x² + 1)³ dx.
questions.explanation: Let u = x² + 1, so du = 2x dx. Then ∫u³du = u⁴/4 + C.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫ x ln x dx.
questions.explanation: Use integration by parts with u=ln x and dv=x dx: (x²/2)ln x - ∫x/2 dx = (x²/2)ln x - x²/4 + C.

questions.question: Which decomposition is correct for 1/[x(x + 1)]?
questions.explanation: Solving 1 = A(x+1) + Bx gives A=1 and B=-1.

questions.question: What makes an improper integral Type I?
options: The interval is finite and the integrand is continuous.
At least one limit of integration is infinite.
questions.explanation: Type I improper integrals extend over an infinite interval.

questions.question: What makes an improper integral Type II?
options: The integrand is unbounded at a point in the interval.
Both limits of integration are infinite.
questions.explanation: Type II improper integrals involve a discontinuity or vertical asymptote within or at an endpoint of a finite interval.

questions.question: For which values of p does ∫₁^∞ 1/xᵖ dx converge?
questions.explanation: The p-integral over [1,∞) converges exactly when p > 1.

questions.question: Evaluate the improper integral ∫₁^∞ 1/x² dx.
questions.explanation: ∫₁^b x⁻²dx = [-1/x]₁^b = 1 - 1/b. Taking b→∞ gives 1.

questions.question: Evaluate the improper integral ∫₀¹ 1/√x dx.
questions.explanation: Write the integrand as x⁻¹/². Its antiderivative is 2√x, giving 2 as the lower limit approaches 0.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the comparison test for improper integrals?
options: Compare the integrand with another nonnegative function whose convergence behaviour is known.
questions.explanation: Bounding an integral by a known convergent or divergent integral can establish its behaviour.

questions.question: Find the area between y = x and y = x² on 0 ≤ x ≤ 1.
Which formula gives the volume by the disk method when y = f(x) is revolved about the x-axis from a to b?
questions.explanation: Each cross-section is a disk of area πr² with radius r=f(x).

questions.question: Which formula describes the washer method?
questions.explanation: A washer's area is the outer disk area minus the inner disk area: πR² - πr².

questions.question: When revolving a region around the y-axis using vertical shells, what is the shell-method formula?
questions.explanation: A cylindrical shell has circumference 2π(radius), height, and thickness dx.

questions.question: Find the volume formed by revolving y = x, 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, about the x-axis.
questions.explanation: Using disks, V = π∫₀¹x²dx = π[x³/3]₀¹ = π/3.

questions.question: Find the volume formed by revolving y = √x, 0 ≤ x ≤ 4, about the x-axis.
questions.explanation: V = π∫₀⁴(√x)²dx = π∫₀⁴x dx = π[x²/2]₀⁴ = 8π.

questions.question: A region bounded by y = 3 and y = 1 is revolved about the x-axis. What are the washer radii?
questions.explanation: Radii are distances from the x-axis: the farther curve gives R=3 and the nearer gives r=1.

questions.question: Find the volume obtained by revolving the region under y = x from x = 0 to x = 1 about the y-axis using shells.
questions.explanation: Shell radius is x and height is x, so V = 2π∫₀¹x²dx = 2π/3.

questions.question: Which step should come first when setting up a volume-of-revolution integral?
options: Sketch the region and identify the axis of revolution.
Evaluate the integral before choosing a method.
questions.explanation: A sketch and the axis determine the appropriate radius, height, bounds, and method.

questions.question: The numerical result of a volume integral should be expressed in what units?
questions.explanation: Volume measures three-dimensional space, so its units are cubed.

questions.question: A particle has velocity v(t) = 3t². What is its displacement from t = 0 to t = 2?
questions.explanation: Displacement = ∫₀²3t²dt = [t³]₀² = 8.

questions.question: Why can total distance travelled differ from displacement?
options: They are identical for every motion.
Distance integrates speed |v(t)|, while displacement integrates signed velocity v(t).
questions.explanation: Negative velocity reduces displacement but still adds positively to total distance.

questions.question: What is the average value of f(x) = x² on [0, 3]?
questions.explanation: Average value = (1/(3-0))∫₀³x²dx = (1/3)(9) = 3.

questions.question: A force F(x) = 2x newtons moves an object from x = 0 to x = 3 metres. How much work is done?
questions.explanation: Work = ∫₀³2x dx = [x²]₀³ = 9 joules.

questions.question: Water enters a tank at a rate r(t) = 5t litres per minute. How much water enters during the first 4 minutes?
questions.explanation: Accumulated volume = ∫₀⁴5t dt = (5/2)(16) = 40 litres.

questions.question: If marginal cost is C'(x) = 4x + 10 and C(0) = 200, what is C(x)?
questions.explanation: Integrate C'(x): C(x)=2x²+10x+K. Since C(0)=200, K=200.

questions.question: If ∫ f(x) dx = x³ + C, what is f(x)?
questions.explanation: Differentiate the antiderivative x³ + C to recover the integrand: f(x)=3x².

questions.question: If f is even, which identity is correct?
questions.explanation: An even function is symmetric about the y-axis, so the two halves contribute equally.

questions.question: A pollutant is discharged at rate r(t) kilograms per hour. What does ∫₀²⁴ r(t)dt represent?
options: The derivative of the discharge rate
The total mass of pollutant discharged in 24 hours
questions.explanation: Integrating a rate over time gives the accumulated quantity.

questions.question: Which integration method is usually most suitable for ∫ x cos x dx?
questions.explanation: The integrand is a product of an algebraic and a trigonometric function, making integration by parts appropriate.
